metadata.formula: \text{residual rotational symmetry}\rightsquigarrow\text{information restriction};\quad\text{target test separation}\rightsquigarrow\text{query lower bound}
metadata.mechanism: Both routes restrict revealed information through orthogonal symmetry and compare it with a target test. The determinant route proves equality of prior-averaged output laws, then Hellinger-amplified radial separation. The eigenbasis route produces an extended joint-law-preserving Krylov representation, then a uniform cosine statistic and target moment bound.
metadata.hypothesis_map: Both use exact matvec, Borel randomized adaptive algorithms, independent seed, worst-case cap, and uniform TV accuracy. Determinant-conditioned product priors and fixed-spectrum Haar rotation are distinct probability experiments. Common sign gives conditional block independence only.
metadata.conclusion_map: Compare organization around an information bottleneck and testing witness. No equivalence of posterior and Krylov lemmas; no automatic epsilon-dependent fixed-spectrum lower bound.
metadata.failure_boundary: Known spectrum is guaranteed only for the eigenbasis route. The sign theorem covers all d,kappa>=4 and epsilon<=1/16; the eigenbasis proof needs fixed delta and large d,kappa<=d^(1-delta). Uniform Krylov saturation and signal/noise ceiling are proof limitations, not a lower bound on possible stronger methods. Expected query costs require an explicit cap/accuracy reduction.

review.scope: Source-intake mechanism correspondence only; no Lean equivalence, certified functor or completed semantic round trip.
